description: Linux, Windows, macOS endpoint and server monitoring — CPU, memory, disk, processes, security events, and compliance.
name: Server & Compute
quickFacts: Deploy Splunk_TA_nix or Splunk_TA_windows on forwarders to start collecting OS metrics immediately.

useCases.title: CPU Utilization Trending (Linux)
useCases.value: Detects overloaded hosts before they cause application degradation. Enables capacity planning and right-sizing.

useCases.title: Memory Pressure Detection (Linux)
useCases.value: Prevents OOM kills, application crashes, and unresponsive systems by detecting memory exhaustion early.

useCases.title: Disk Capacity Forecasting (Linux)
useCases.value: Prevents outages caused by full filesystems. A full /var or / can bring down services, databases, and logging. Enables proactive storage procurement.

useCases.title: Disk I/O Saturation (Linux)
useCases.value: High I/O wait degrades application performance even when CPU and memory look healthy. Catches storage bottlenecks before users complain.

useCases.title: System Load Anomalies
useCases.value: Load average exceeding CPU core count indicates process queuing. Useful as an early warning for runaway processes or unexpected workloads.

useCases.title: Process Crash Detection (Linux)
useCases.value: Immediate awareness of unexpected process terminations. Critical for services that don't auto-restart or have no watchdog.

useCases.title: OOM Killer Events
useCases.value: OOM killer invocations mean the system ran out of memory and Linux chose to kill a process to survive. This often takes out critical services silently.

useCases.title: SSH Brute-Force Detection
useCases.value: Detects active password-guessing attacks against SSH services. Can be early indicator of compromised credentials or targeted intrusion attempts.

useCases.title: Unauthorized Sudo Usage
useCases.value: Repeated failed `sudo` attempts indicate attacker probing after account compromise; unexpected `sudo` success with destructive commands (e.g. `rm -rf`, `chmod 777`) may signal insider misuse or stole…

useCases.title: Cron Job Failure Monitoring
useCases.value: Failed cron jobs can silently break batch processing, backups, log rotation, and maintenance tasks. Catching failures early prevents cascading issues.

useCases.title: Kernel Panic Detection
useCases.value: Kernel panics cause immediate system crashes and potential data corruption. Often indicates hardware failure, driver issues, or memory corruption.

useCases.title: NTP Time Sync Drift (Linux)
useCases.value: Clock drift causes authentication failures (Kerberos), log correlation issues, transaction ordering problems, and certificate validation failures.

useCases.title: Zombie Process Accumulation
useCases.value: Zombie processes indicate parent processes not properly reaping children. Accumulation can exhaust PID space and indicates application bugs.

useCases.title: File Descriptor Exhaustion
useCases.value: File descriptor exhaustion causes "too many open files" errors, breaking network connections, log writing, and inter-process communication. Common in Java apps and databases.

useCases.title: Network Interface Errors
useCases.value: Interface errors (CRC, drops, overruns) indicate bad cables, failing NICs, or duplex mismatches. Catching early prevents intermittent application failures.

useCases.title: Package Vulnerability Tracking
useCases.value: Maintains visibility into known vulnerable packages across the fleet, supporting vulnerability management and compliance programs.

useCases.title: Service Availability Monitoring
useCases.value: Detects stopped services before users notice. Essential for any SLA-bound service where uptime matters.

useCases.title: User Account Changes
useCases.value: Detects unauthorized user creation or modification. Key for security auditing and compliance (SOX, PCI, HIPAA).

useCases.title: Filesystem Read-Only Detection
useCases.value: A filesystem remounting as read-only indicates disk failure, corruption, or mount issues. Applications will fail silently when they can't write.

useCases.title: Reboot Detection (Linux)
useCases.value: Unexpected reboots may indicate kernel panics, hardware failure, or unauthorized changes. Distinguishing planned vs. unplanned reboots is key.

useCases.title: Kernel Module Loading Tracking
useCases.value: Detects unauthorized kernel module insertions which can indicate rootkits or malware persistence.

useCases.title: Sysctl Parameter Changes Detection
useCases.value: Identifies modifications to kernel parameters that affect system behavior, security posture, or performance tuning.

useCases.title: Kernel Core Dump Generation
useCases.value: Core dumps indicate process crashes at kernel level, enabling root cause analysis of system stability issues.

useCases.title: Kernel Ring Buffer Error Rate
useCases.value: Ring buffer errors signal kernel-level problems including driver issues, hardware failures, or module conflicts.

useCases.title: NUMA Imbalance Detection
useCases.value: NUMA imbalance causes memory locality issues and performance degradation on multi-socket systems.

useCases.title: CPU Frequency Scaling Events
useCases.value: Frequency scaling changes indicate thermal throttling or power management adjustments affecting workload performance.

useCases.title: CPU Steal Time Elevation (Virtual Machines)
useCases.value: High steal time indicates VM is contending with host resources, affecting application performance.

useCases.title: IRQ Imbalance Across CPU Cores
useCases.value: Imbalanced IRQ handling causes uneven CPU utilization and can bottleneck network or storage throughput.

useCases.title: Context Switch Rate Anomaly Detection (Linux)
useCases.value: Excessive context switching reduces CPU cache effectiveness and indicates scheduler overload or contention.

useCases.title: Scheduler Latency and Run Queue Depth
useCases.value: High run queue depth with elevated scheduling latency causes visible application performance degradation.

useCases.title: Hugepage Allocation and Usage
useCases.value: Hugepage contention or allocation failures impact database and large memory workload performance.

useCases.title: Transparent Hugepage Compaction Stalls
useCases.value: THP compaction stalls indicate severe memory fragmentation affecting latency-sensitive workloads.

useCases.title: Inode Exhaustion Detection
useCases.value: Inode exhaustion causes file creation failures even when disk space remains available, stopping applications.

useCases.title: RAID Array Degradation Detection
useCases.value: Degraded RAID arrays mean data loss risk and potential performance impact during rebuild.

useCases.title: LVM Thin Pool Capacity Monitoring
useCases.value: Thin pool exhaustion causes I/O errors on all logical volumes in the pool, causing application failures.

useCases.title: Multipath I/O Failover Events
useCases.value: Multipath failovers indicate storage path degradation requiring immediate investigation to prevent I/O loss.

useCases.title: NFS Mount Stale Handle Detection
useCases.value: Stale NFS handles cause application hangs and I/O failures that severely impact users.

useCases.title: Filesystem Journal Errors
useCases.value: Filesystem journal errors indicate potential corruption risk and can lead to data loss or recovery timeouts.

useCases.title: Ext4 Filesystem Errors and Recovery
useCases.value: Ext4 errors may indicate filesystem corruption or hardware issues requiring immediate diagnostic action.

useCases.title: XFS Filesystem Errors and Recovery
useCases.value: XFS errors indicate potential corruption in high-performance storage systems commonly used in enterprise environments.

useCases.title: Disk SMART Health Monitoring
useCases.value: SMART errors predict disk failure, enabling proactive replacement before data loss occurs.

useCases.title: SSD Wear Leveling and Health
useCases.value: SSD wear metrics indicate remaining lifespan, enabling proactive replacement planning.

useCases.title: Fstrim and TRIM Command Monitoring
useCases.value: Fstrim failures indicate potential SSD performance degradation from lack of proper space reclamation.

useCases.title: Memory Leak Detection Per Process
useCases.value: Process memory leaks cause gradual performance degradation and eventual OOM situations.

useCases.title: Swap Thrashing Detection
useCases.value: Swap thrashing causes severe performance degradation and can make systems unresponsive.

useCases.title: Slab Cache Growth Monitoring
useCases.value: Unbounded slab cache growth consumes memory that could be used for page cache or application memory.

useCases.title: Page Cache Pressure and Reclaim Activity
useCases.value: High page cache reclaim activity indicates memory pressure affecting application performance.

useCases.title: NUMA Memory Imbalance Per Node
useCases.value: NUMA memory imbalance causes remote memory access latency affecting NUMA-aware applications.

useCases.title: Memory Cgroup Limit Enforcement
useCases.value: Cgroup limits prevent runaway processes but enforcement indicates containers at memory limits need scaling.

useCases.title: Transparent Hugepage Defragmentation Stalls
useCases.value: THP defrag stalls cause application latency spikes affecting real-time and interactive workloads.

useCases.title: TCP Retransmission Rate Elevation
useCases.value: High retransmission rates indicate network congestion, packet loss, or application issues affecting throughput.

useCases.title: Connection Tracking Table Exhaustion
useCases.value: Conntrack table full prevents new network connections, causing application failures.

useCases.title: Socket Buffer Overflow Detection
useCases.value: Socket buffer overflows cause packet drops and connection resets, indicating network saturation or misconfiguration.

useCases.title: Network Namespace Monitoring
useCases.value: Network namespace monitoring detects container escape attempts and validates network isolation in containerized environments.

useCases.title: DNS Resolution Failure Rate
useCases.value: DNS failures impact application availability and user experience, requiring immediate investigation.

useCases.title: Firewall Rule Hit Tracking (iptables/nftables)
useCases.value: Firewall rule tracking identifies blocked traffic patterns, helping optimize rules and detect attack attempts.

useCases.title: ARP Table Overflow Detection
useCases.value: ARP table overflow causes network connectivity issues and may indicate ARP spoofing attacks or network misconfiguration.

useCases.title: Network Bond Failover Events (Linux)
useCases.value: Network bond failovers indicate NIC or port failures requiring immediate remediation to prevent connectivity loss.

useCases.title: Network Team Failover Detection (Linux)
useCases.value: Teamed interface failovers indicate critical network path failures affecting server connectivity.

useCases.title: MTU Mismatch Detection
useCases.value: MTU mismatches cause fragmentation and performance issues, especially with jumbo frame configurations.

useCases.title: TCP TIME_WAIT Accumulation
useCases.value: Excessive TIME_WAIT sockets can exhaust ephemeral port space, causing connection failures under load.

useCases.title: Network Bandwidth Utilization by Interface (Linux)
useCases.value: High bandwidth utilization indicates potential capacity constraints or unexpected traffic patterns.

useCases.title: Dropped Packets by Network Interface
useCases.value: Dropped packets indicate network issues, buffer overflow, or driver problems affecting reliability.

useCases.title: Network Latency Monitoring (Ping RTT)
useCases.value: Elevated latency to critical services impacts application performance and user experience.

useCases.title: Auditd Rule Violation Detection
useCases.value: Auditd violations provide forensic evidence of security incidents and unauthorized system access.

useCases.title: SELinux Denial Monitoring
useCases.value: SELinux denials indicate policy violations that may require tuning or signal legitimate attack attempts.

useCases.title: AppArmor Profile Violation Detection
useCases.value: AppArmor violations indicate policy breaches that may reflect policy misconfigurations or attack attempts.

useCases.title: Rootkit Detection via File Integrity
useCases.value: File integrity changes indicate potential rootkit installation or unauthorized system modification.

useCases.title: SUID/SGID Binary Changes
useCases.value: Unauthorized SUID/SGID binary modifications enable privilege escalation attacks.

useCases.title: /etc/passwd Modifications
useCases.value: /etc/passwd changes indicate user account creation/modification requiring immediate investigation for unauthorized access.

useCases.title: /etc/shadow Modifications
useCases.value: /etc/shadow changes indicate password hash tampering or unauthorized privilege escalation attempts.

useCases.title: SSH Public Key Changes
useCases.value: SSH key modifications enable persistent unauthorized access, indicating potential account compromise.

useCases.title: PAM Authentication Failure Tracking
useCases.value: PAM failures indicate authentication issues or brute-force attack attempts against user accounts.

useCases.title: Login from Unusual Source IPs
useCases.value: Logins from unusual source IPs may indicate account compromise or unauthorized access.

useCases.title: Failed su Attempts
useCases.value: Failed su attempts indicate potential privilege escalation attempts or credential compromise.

useCases.title: Privilege Escalation Detection
useCases.value: Privilege escalation indicates successful security breach enabling attacker to gain administrative access.

useCases.title: Unauthorized Cron Job Additions
useCases.value: Unauthorized cron jobs enable persistent malware execution and data exfiltration.

useCases.title: Open Port Changes
useCases.value: New listening ports indicate service configuration changes or malware opening backdoors.

useCases.title: Setcap Binary Monitoring
useCases.value: Setcap binary modifications enable privilege escalation bypassing traditional privilege boundary enforcement.

useCases.title: Systemd Unit Failures
useCases.value: Service unit failures indicate application issues or configuration problems requiring immediate remediation.

useCases.title: Systemd Timer Missed Triggers
useCases.value: Missed systemd timers indicate scheduling issues or system overload preventing scheduled tasks.

useCases.title: D-State (Uninterruptible Sleep) Process Detection
useCases.value: D-state processes indicate hanging I/O operations or kernel deadlocks requiring immediate investigation.

useCases.title: Process CPU Affinity Changes
useCases.value: CPU affinity changes can indicate attempted performance optimization or malicious CPU isolation attempts.

useCases.title: Runaway Process Detection (CPU Hog)
useCases.value: Runaway processes consuming excessive CPU degrade performance for all workloads on the host.

useCases.title: Memory Hog Detection
useCases.value: Memory-consuming processes can cause OOM conditions affecting all applications on the host.

useCases.title: Fork Bomb Detection
useCases.value: Fork bombs exhaust PID space and system resources, making systems unusable.

useCases.title: Process Namespace Breakout Detection
useCases.value: Process namespace breakout indicates container escape or privilege escalation enabling access to host.

useCases.title: Container Escape Attempt Detection
useCases.value: Container escape attempts are critical security events indicating sophisticated attack against containerized infrastructure.

useCases.title: Syslog Flood Detection
useCases.value: Syslog floods can overwhelm log infrastructure and mask real security events in log noise.

useCases.title: Journal Disk Usage Monitoring
useCases.value: Journal disk usage growth can consume valuable storage space, potentially filling disks.

useCases.title: Log Rotation Failures
useCases.value: Log rotation failures can cause log files to grow unbounded, consuming disk space and impacting log analysis.

useCases.title: Auditd Daemon Health
useCases.value: Auditd daemon failure results in loss of security audit trail, creating compliance and forensic gaps.

useCases.title: Rsyslog Queue Backlog Monitoring
useCases.value: Rsyslog queue backlog indicates log forwarding issues or overload of remote syslog infrastructure.

useCases.title: Failed Log Forwarding
useCases.value: Failed log forwarding creates data loss in centralized logging infrastructure, creating gaps in monitoring and compliance.

useCases.title: TCP Connection Establishment Rate
useCases.value: High connection establishment rate may indicate application behavior changes or DDoS attack preparation.

useCases.title: NUMA Hit/Miss Ratio Tracking
useCases.value: Tracking NUMA hit/miss ratio identifies opportunities for workload optimization on NUMA systems.

useCases.title: CPU C-State Residency Monitoring
useCases.value: CPU C-state residency tracking optimizes power consumption and identifies power management issues.

useCases.title: TLB Shootdown Rate Monitoring
useCases.value: High TLB shootdown rates indicate excessive cross-CPU cache invalidations affecting performance on multi-CPU systems.

useCases.title: Kernel Lock Contention Detection
useCases.value: Kernel lock contention degrades multi-core scalability and application throughput.

useCases.title: Softirq Rate Monitoring
useCases.value: High softirq rates indicate kernel workload distribution issues or network stack pressure.

useCases.title: Context Switch Anomalies Detection
useCases.value: Context switch anomalies indicate scheduler issues or unexpected process workload changes.

useCases.title: EDAC Memory Error Tracking
useCases.value: EDAC memory errors indicate hardware failures predicting imminent memory or system failure.

useCases.title: IPMI Sensor Threshold Violations
useCases.value: IPMI sensor violations indicate hardware conditions (thermal, voltage, power) requiring immediate remediation.

useCases.title: Thermal Throttling Detection
useCases.value: Thermal throttling reduces CPU performance to prevent overheating, indicating cooling system issues.

useCases.title: Fan Speed Anomalies
useCases.value: Fan speed anomalies indicate cooling system degradation potentially leading to thermal overload.

useCases.title: Power Supply State Changes
useCases.value: Power supply state changes indicate hardware failures requiring immediate physical intervention.

useCases.title: Hardware Clock Drift Detection
useCases.value: Hardware clock drift affects system time accuracy impacting application consistency and audit trails.

useCases.title: Password Policy Violation Detection
useCases.value: Password policy violations indicate accounts with weak credentials vulnerable to compromise.

useCases.title: Account Expiry Monitoring
useCases.value: Account expiry tracking ensures user accounts remain valid and prevents access with expired credentials.

useCases.title: Inactive User Detection
useCases.value: Inactive users with enabled accounts represent security risk and should be disabled to reduce attack surface.

useCases.title: World-Writable File Detection
useCases.value: World-writable files can be modified by any user enabling privilege escalation or system compromise.

useCases.title: Unowned File Detection
useCases.value: Unowned files indicate potential file system corruption or security issue requiring investigation.

useCases.title: SETUID Audit and Tracking
useCases.value: SETUID binary execution enables privilege escalation requiring tracking for security monitoring.

useCases.title: Open File Handle Per-Process Monitoring
useCases.value: High open file handle counts per process can exhaust system limits causing application failures.

useCases.title: Listening Port Compliance
useCases.value: Port compliance ensures only authorized services are listening, reducing attack surface.

useCases.title: Installed Package Drift Detection
useCases.value: Package drift indicates unauthorized software installation or configuration management failures.

useCases.title: Configuration File Change Tracking (/etc)
useCases.value: Configuration file changes can indicate system compromise or unauthorized configuration modifications.

useCases.title: System Reboot Frequency Anomaly
useCases.value: Unexpected reboot frequency indicates system instability, crashes, or possible security incident response.

useCases.title: Defunct (Zombie) Process Accumulation
useCases.value: Accumulating zombie processes indicate application resource leaks causing process table exhaustion risk.

useCases.title: Symbolic Link Chain Depth Monitoring
useCases.value: Excessive symbolic link chains can cause performance issues and may indicate directory traversal vulnerabilities.

useCases.title: Bootloader Configuration Changes
useCases.value: Bootloader changes can enable persistence mechanisms or bypass security controls at boot time.

useCases.title: Systemd Unit State Monitoring
useCases.value: Track failed/inactive systemd services, auto-restart counts, and service startup time to prevent cascading failures and identify misconfigured or unhealthy units.

useCases.title: Linux Cgroup Resource Pressure (PSI)
useCases.value: Monitor Pressure Stall Information (PSI) for CPU, memory, and I/O at cgroup level to detect resource contention before it causes application latency.

useCases.title: Linux Entropy Pool Depletion
useCases.value: Low entropy blocks /dev/random and can stall crypto operations (SSL handshakes, key generation). Detecting depletion prevents application hangs and security failures.

useCases.title: Linux Journal / Journald Health
useCases.value: Journal corruption, excessive disk usage, and rate-limited entries indicate logging problems that can hide critical events and fill disk.

useCases.title: Chrony / NTP Time Synchronization Drift
useCases.value: Clock offset, stratum, and reachability issues cause authentication failures, log correlation errors, and certificate validation problems. Time drift is a root cause of many subtle failures.

useCases.title: Swap Activity Rate Trending
useCases.value: Pages swapped in/out per second (distinct from swap usage %) indicates memory pressure and I/O load. High swap I/O rate degrades performance even before swap usage is critical.

useCases.title: Filesystem Inode Exhaustion
useCases.value: Inode usage approaching 100% blocks file creation even with free disk space. Applications fail with "No space left on device" despite available blocks — a common misdiagnosis.

useCases.title: Linux Softirq / Hardirq Time
useCases.value: Detect interrupt storms (softirq/hardirq) that degrade system performance. High IRQ time indicates network, block I/O, or timer storms.

useCases.title: TCP Connection State Distribution (Linux)
useCases.value: Count of ESTABLISHED, TIME_WAIT, CLOSE_WAIT, SYN_RECV connections. Detects connection leaks (accumulating CLOSE_WAIT), exhaustion (TIME_WAIT), and half-open buildup.

useCases.title: Linux OOM Killer Invocation Tracking
useCases.value: Track which processes were killed by the OOM killer and how often. OOM events indicate severe memory pressure and often precede application outages.

useCases.title: CPU Utilization Trending (Windows)
useCases.value: Sustained high CPU causes application timeouts and service degradation. Trending enables capacity planning and helps identify runaway processes.

useCases.title: Memory Utilization & Paging (Windows)
useCases.value: High memory and excessive paging degrade performance. Page file usage indicates the system is under memory pressure.

useCases.title: Disk Space Monitoring (Windows)
useCases.value: Full disks crash applications, stop logging, and corrupt databases. Windows can become unbootable if the system drive fills.

useCases.title: Windows Service Failures
useCases.value: Stopped critical services directly impact application availability. Auto-restart doesn't always work, and some services can't auto-restart.

useCases.title: Event Log Flood Detection
useCases.value: Abnormal event log volumes often indicate error loops, misconfiguration, or an active attack. Also protects Splunk license from unexpected spikes.

useCases.title: Failed Login Monitoring
useCases.value: Detects credential stuffing, brute-force attacks, and compromised account usage. Key for security monitoring and compliance.

useCases.title: Account Lockout Tracking
useCases.value: Lockouts frustrate users and can indicate active attacks. Identifying the source computer of the lockout dramatically speeds resolution.

useCases.title: Privileged Group Changes
useCases.value: Additions to Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, or Schema Admins grant extreme privilege. Unauthorized changes could mean full domain compromise.

useCases.title: Windows Update Compliance
useCases.value: Unpatched systems are primary attack vectors. Tracking patch compliance across the fleet supports vulnerability management and regulatory requirements.

useCases.title: Scheduled Task Failures
useCases.value: Failed scheduled tasks break batch jobs, cleanup scripts, and automated processes. Often goes unnoticed until downstream effects appear.

useCases.title: Blue Screen of Death (BSOD)
useCases.value: BSODs indicate severe system instability — driver bugs, hardware failure, or memory corruption. Repeated BSODs on the same host demand immediate attention.

useCases.title: RDP Session Monitoring
useCases.value: Tracks who connected via Remote Desktop, from where, and when. Essential for compliance auditing and detecting lateral movement.

useCases.title: PowerShell Script Execution
useCases.value: PowerShell is the most common tool in modern Windows attacks (Cobalt Strike, Empire, fileless malware). Script block logging captures the actual code executed.

useCases.title: DNS Server Health
useCases.value: DNS is foundational infrastructure — when DNS is slow or failing, everything fails. Monitoring query rates and failures ensures resolution reliability.

useCases.title: DHCP Scope Exhaustion
useCases.value: When DHCP scopes run out of addresses, new devices can't get network access. Often manifests as "network down" complaints.

useCases.title: Certificate Expiration
useCases.value: Expired certificates cause TLS failures, broken websites, authentication failures, and service outages. Among the most preventable outage causes.

useCases.title: Group Policy Processing Failures
useCases.value: GPO failures mean security policies, drive mappings, software deployments, and configurations aren't being applied. Systems may be running with stale or missing policies.

useCases.title: Print Spooler Issues
useCases.value: Print spooler crashes affect print services and have historically been attack vectors (PrintNightmare). Monitoring catches both operational and security issues.

useCases.title: Disk I/O Queue Length (Windows)
useCases.value: Sustained high disk queue lengths indicate storage bottlenecks invisible to CPU/memory monitoring. Causes application hangs and timeout errors.

useCases.title: Process Handle Leak Detection
useCases.value: Handle leaks cause resource exhaustion and eventual application crashes or system instability. Detecting the leak early prevents unplanned outages.

useCases.title: Non-Paged Pool Exhaustion
useCases.value: Non-paged pool memory is limited kernel memory. Exhaustion causes BSOD (DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL). Often caused by driver leaks.

useCases.title: Network Interface Utilization (Windows)
useCases.value: Saturated network interfaces cause packet drops, retransmissions, and application timeouts. Often missed when only CPU/memory are monitored.

useCases.title: Processor Queue Length
useCases.value: Processor queue length >2 per core indicates threads waiting for CPU time. Detects CPU contention even when average utilization looks normal due to burst patterns.

useCases.title: Security Log Cleared
useCases.value: Clearing the Security event log is a classic attacker technique to cover tracks. Legitimate clears are rare and should always be investigated.

useCases.title: New Service Installation
useCases.value: Attackers install malicious services for persistence. Unexpected service installations outside change windows indicate compromise or unauthorized software.

useCases.title: Windows Firewall Rule Changes
useCases.value: Unauthorized firewall rule changes can open attack vectors. Malware often disables the firewall or adds allow rules for C2 communication.

useCases.title: Registry Run Key Modification (Persistence)
useCases.value: Run/RunOnce registry keys are the most common malware persistence mechanism. Monitoring these keys catches many threats early.

useCases.title: LSASS Memory Access (Credential Dumping)
useCases.value: Accessing LSASS process memory is the primary technique for credential theft (Mimikatz, ProcDump). Detection is critical to stopping lateral movement.

useCases.title: Kerberos Authentication Failures
useCases.value: Kerberos failures (EventCode 4771) reveal password spraying, expired accounts, clock skew, and misconfigured SPNs. Distinct from NTLM failures and requires separate monitoring.

useCases.title: WMI Event Subscription Persistence
useCases.value: WMI event subscriptions are a stealthy persistence mechanism that survives reboots. Used by APT groups and fileless malware.

useCases.title: Audit Policy Changes
useCases.value: Attackers modify audit policies to disable logging and hide their activities. Any unauthorized audit policy change must be investigated immediately.

useCases.title: AppLocker / WDAC Policy Violations
useCases.value: AppLocker/WDAC blocks track unauthorized application execution attempts. High violation rates indicate persistent threats or misconfigured policies.

useCases.title: Windows Defender Threat Detections
useCases.value: Real-time visibility into endpoint AV detections across the fleet. Delayed response to malware detections increases blast radius.

useCases.title: DCSync Attack Detection
useCases.value: DCSync uses Directory Replication Service permissions to extract password hashes remotely. Detecting non-DC replication requests catches this attack before credential theft completes.

useCases.title: Kerberoasting Detection (SPN Ticket Requests)
useCases.value: Kerberoasting requests TGS tickets for service accounts with SPNs, then cracks them offline. Detecting anomalous TGS requests catches this before passwords are compromised.

useCases.title: AD Object Deletion Monitoring
useCases.value: Accidental or malicious deletion of AD objects (OUs, users, groups, computer accounts) can cause widespread service disruption. AD Recycle Bin has a limited window.

useCases.title: Domain Trust Changes
useCases.value: Unauthorized trust relationships can grant external domains access to internal resources. Trust modifications are rare and high-impact.

useCases.title: WHEA Hardware Error Reporting
useCases.value: Windows Hardware Error Architecture (WHEA) reports CPU, memory, and PCIe hardware errors before they cause crashes. Enables proactive hardware replacement.

useCases.title: Volume Shadow Copy Failures
useCases.value: VSS failures break backup chains, System Restore, and SQL/Exchange application-consistent snapshots. Often silent until a restore is attempted.

useCases.title: .NET CLR Performance Monitoring
useCases.value: .NET garbage collection pauses and high exception rates cause application latency and instability. CLR monitoring reveals issues invisible to external health checks.

useCases.title: Failover Cluster Event Monitoring
useCases.value: Cluster failovers indicate node failures or network partitions affecting high-availability services. Each failover risks brief downtime and potential data loss.

useCases.title: SMB Share Access Anomalies
useCases.value: Anomalous SMB share access patterns indicate lateral movement, data exfiltration, or ransomware file encryption across network shares.

useCases.title: Windows Time Service (W32Time) Issues
useCases.value: Time synchronization failures break Kerberos authentication (5-minute tolerance), cause log correlation issues, and invalidate audit trails.

useCases.title: DFS-R Replication Backlog
useCases.value: DFS-R replication backlogs mean file servers are out of sync. Users may access stale data, and a prolonged backlog can trigger an initial sync (full re-replication).

useCases.title: Application Crash (WER) Trending
useCases.value: Windows Error Reporting captures crash details for all applications. Trending reveals systemic instability, bad patches, or problematic application versions.

useCases.title: PowerShell Script Block Logging
useCases.value: Script Block Logging captures the full text of every PowerShell script executed, including deobfuscated code. Essential for detecting fileless attacks and encoded commands.

useCases.title: Lateral Movement via Explicit Credentials
useCases.value: Logon type 9 (NewCredentials / RunAs /netonly) and type 10 (RDP) from unexpected sources reveal credential abuse and lateral movement between systems.

useCases.title: DNS Debug Query Logging
useCases.value: DNS query logging reveals C2 communication via DNS tunneling, DGA domains, and unauthorized DNS resolution. Essential for security visibility.

useCases.title: Process Creation with Command Line Auditing
useCases.value: Full command-line visibility on process creation is the foundation of threat detection. Reveals encoded PowerShell, LOLBin abuse, and suspicious child processes.

useCases.title: NIC Teaming / LBFO Failover (Windows)
useCases.value: NIC team member failures reduce redundancy silently. A second failure causes full network loss. Detecting the first failure enables proactive repair.

useCases.title: BitLocker Recovery Events
useCases.value: BitLocker recovery mode triggers indicate TPM issues, boot configuration changes, or potential tampering with the boot chain. Each event requires investigation.

useCases.title: Windows Event Forwarding (WEF) Health
useCases.value: WEF collects events from thousands of endpoints to central collectors. Forwarding failures create visibility gaps across the security monitoring pipeline.

useCases.title: Suspicious Token Manipulation
useCases.value: Token impersonation and privilege escalation via token manipulation (SeImpersonatePrivilege abuse) is a common post-exploitation technique.

useCases.title: Sysmon Network Connection Monitoring
useCases.value: Sysmon EventCode 3 logs every outbound TCP/UDP connection with the originating process. Reveals C2 callbacks, data exfiltration, and unauthorized network access.

useCases.title: Thread Count Exhaustion
useCases.value: Thread leaks or excessive thread creation cause pool exhaustion and application hangs. Windows has a system-wide limit of ~65K threads that affects all processes.

useCases.title: Storage Spaces Health Monitoring
useCases.value: Storage Spaces pools degrade silently when physical disks fail. Detection before a second disk fails prevents data loss in mirrored/parity configurations.

useCases.title: DCOM / COM+ Application Errors
useCases.value: DCOM errors affect distributed applications, WMI remote management, and MMC snap-ins. Persistent errors indicate permission issues or component registration corruption.

useCases.title: Code Integrity / Driver Signing Violations
useCases.value: Unsigned or tampered drivers loading into the kernel are a rootkit indicator. Code Integrity violations detect bypass attempts and driver-level threats.

useCases.title: Data Deduplication Health
useCases.value: Windows Data Deduplication saves significant storage on file servers. Job failures or savings degradation indicate volume corruption or configuration issues.

useCases.title: TCP Connection State Monitoring (Windows)
useCases.value: Excessive TIME_WAIT, CLOSE_WAIT, or ESTABLISHED connections indicate connection leaks, exhausted ephemeral ports, or application hanging. Causes service unavailability.

useCases.title: Windows Installer Failures
useCases.value: MSI installation failures affect patching, software deployment, and SCCM/Intune compliance. Repeated failures indicate corrupted Windows Installer service or disk issues.

useCases.title: Event Log Channel Size / Overflow
useCases.value: When event logs reach maximum size with overwrite-oldest policy, critical security events are lost. With do-not-overwrite policy, the log stops recording entirely.

useCases.title: Pass-the-Hash / NTLM Relay Detection
useCases.value: Pass-the-hash attacks use stolen NTLM hashes to authenticate without knowing the password. Detecting NTLM logons from unusual sources catches this common lateral movement technique.

useCases.title: Sysmon File Creation in Suspicious Paths
useCases.value: Files created in temp directories, startup folders, and system paths by unexpected processes indicate malware dropping payloads or establishing persistence.

useCases.title: Golden Ticket Detection (TGT Anomalies)
useCases.value: Golden tickets are forged Kerberos TGTs that grant domain-wide access. Detecting anomalous TGT properties catches this catastrophic compromise.

useCases.title: NTFS Corruption and Self-Healing
useCases.value: NTFS corruption can cause data loss, application failures, and boot issues. Self-healing events indicate disk degradation that will worsen.

useCases.title: Page File Usage & Exhaustion
useCases.value: Page file exhaustion prevents new process creation and causes "out of virtual memory" errors. System-managed page files can grow to fill the disk.

useCases.title: Context Switch Rate Anomalies (Windows)
useCases.value: Abnormally high context switch rates indicate excessive threading, poor application design, or kernel-mode driver issues. Degrades overall system performance.

useCases.title: Scheduled Task Creation (Persistence)
useCases.value: Scheduled tasks are a common persistence mechanism for malware. New tasks created outside change management warrant investigation.

useCases.title: WinRM / Remote PowerShell Connections
useCases.value: WinRM enables remote command execution via PowerShell Remoting. Monitoring inbound WinRM sessions detects lateral movement and unauthorized remote management.

useCases.title: LDAP Query Performance (DC Health)
useCases.value: Slow LDAP queries on domain controllers degrade authentication, group policy processing, and application lookups across the entire domain.

useCases.title: AdminSDHolder Modification
useCases.value: The AdminSDHolder container controls ACLs on all privileged AD groups. Modifying it grants persistent hidden admin access that survives permission resets.

useCases.title: SPN Modification (Targeted Kerberoasting)
useCases.value: Attackers add SPNs to admin accounts to make them Kerberoastable. Monitoring SPN changes on sensitive accounts catches this setup before the actual attack.

useCases.title: DSRM Account Usage
useCases.value: The Directory Services Restore Mode (DSRM) account is a local admin on every DC with a rarely-changed password. Its use outside restores indicates compromise.

useCases.title: Sysmon DNS Query Logging
useCases.value: Per-process DNS query logging reveals which applications communicate with which domains. Detects DGA, C2 callbacks, and data exfiltration at the endpoint level.

useCases.title: SMBv1 Usage Detection
useCases.value: SMBv1 is vulnerable to EternalBlue and WannaCry. Detecting remaining SMBv1 traffic identifies systems that need upgrading or have SMBv1 re-enabled.

useCases.title: Credential Guard Status Monitoring
useCases.value: Credential Guard protects NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets in an isolated container. Monitoring ensures it remains enabled and isn't bypassed.

useCases.title: Boot Configuration Changes (BCDEdit)
useCases.value: Boot configuration changes can disable Secure Boot, enable test signing (rootkit loading), or modify boot chain integrity. Used by advanced threats.

useCases.title: Sysmon Named Pipe Monitoring
useCases.value: Named pipes are used for inter-process communication and by tools like Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, and PsExec. Detecting unusual named pipes reveals C2 and lateral movement.

useCases.title: NTLM Audit and Restriction Monitoring
useCases.value: NTLM is a legacy authentication protocol vulnerable to relay attacks. Auditing NTLM usage identifies applications and systems that need migration to Kerberos.

useCases.title: DPAPI Credential Backup (DC)
useCases.value: Data Protection API master key backup to domain controllers enables credential theft. Abnormal DPAPI backup activity from unexpected accounts indicates compromise.

useCases.title: Windows Search Indexer Issues
useCases.value: Search Indexer crashes and high resource usage affect file server performance and SharePoint crawling. Index corruption requires full rebuild.

useCases.title: System Uptime & Unexpected Restarts (Windows)
useCases.value: Unexpected restarts indicate BSOD, power loss, forced reboots, or patch installations. Tracking uptime reveals instability patterns and unauthorized maintenance.

useCases.title: Shadow Copy Deletion (Ransomware Indicator)
useCases.value: Ransomware deletes volume shadow copies to prevent file recovery. Detecting vssadmin/wmic shadow deletion commands is a high-confidence ransomware indicator.

useCases.title: USB / Removable Device Auditing
useCases.value: Removable storage devices are a data exfiltration vector. Auditing device connections enables DLP and compliance enforcement.

useCases.title: Remote Desktop Gateway Session Monitoring
useCases.value: RD Gateway is the entry point for remote workers. Monitoring session lifecycle detects unauthorized access, session hijacking, and resource abuse.

useCases.title: Group Policy Object (GPO) Modification Auditing
useCases.value: GPO changes affect all domain-joined systems. Unauthorized GPO modifications can deploy malware, weaken security, or exfiltrate credentials at scale.

useCases.title: Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) Activity
useCases.value: WSL can be abused to run Linux-based attack tools while evading Windows-focused security tooling. Monitoring WSL activity closes this visibility gap.

useCases.title: Windows Container Health Monitoring
useCases.value: Windows containers running on Server 2019+ need monitoring for resource limits, failures, and networking issues to ensure application availability.

useCases.title: DNS Server Zone Transfer Monitoring
useCases.value: Zone transfers expose the entire DNS namespace to attackers. Unauthorized zone transfers enable reconnaissance and must be detected immediately.

useCases.title: Print Spooler Vulnerability Monitoring (PrintNightmare)
useCases.value: Print Spooler vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-34527, CVE-2021-1675) enable remote code execution and privilege escalation. Continuous monitoring ensures patches hold and exploitation attempts are caught.

useCases.title: NPS / RADIUS Authentication Monitoring
useCases.value: Network Policy Server handles VPN, Wi-Fi, and 802.1X authentication. Monitoring NPS detects brute-force attacks, misconfigured policies, and unauthorized network access.

useCases.title: PKI / Certificate Authority Health
useCases.value: An enterprise CA issues certificates for authentication, encryption, and code signing. CA failures break SSO, VPN, Wi-Fi, and TLS across the organization.

useCases.title: File Share Access Auditing (SMB)
useCases.value: File share access auditing detects unauthorized data access, lateral movement via mapped drives, and ransomware encrypting network shares.

useCases.title: Software Restriction / AppLocker Bypass Detection
useCases.value: Application whitelisting is a primary defense against malware. Detecting bypass attempts reveals both sophisticated attackers and policy gaps.

useCases.title: Terminal Services / RDP Session Tracking
useCases.value: RDP is a primary lateral movement vector. Complete session tracking from logon to logoff enables detection of compromised credentials and unauthorized access.

useCases.title: Disk Latency and I/O Performance (Windows)
useCases.value: High disk latency directly impacts application performance and user experience. Proactive monitoring prevents performance degradation and identifies failing storage.

useCases.title: Windows Defender Exclusion Monitoring
useCases.value: Attackers add Defender exclusions to hide malware. Monitoring exclusion changes detects evasion techniques and ensures antivirus coverage remains complete.

useCases.title: Local Administrator Group Membership Changes
useCases.value: Local admin privileges enable credential theft, persistence, and lateral movement. Monitoring local admin group changes detects privilege escalation attacks.

useCases.title: DFS Replication Health Monitoring
useCases.value: DFS-R synchronizes SYSVOL and shared folders across domain controllers and file servers. Replication failures cause inconsistent GPOs and stale data.

useCases.title: Kerberos Constrained Delegation Abuse
useCases.value: Kerberos delegation allows services to impersonate users. Misconfigured or compromised delegation targets enable privilege escalation to domain admin.

useCases.title: Windows Time Service (W32Time) Drift
useCases.value: Kerberos authentication fails when clock skew exceeds 5 minutes. Time drift breaks authentication, log correlation, and forensic timelines.

useCases.title: PowerShell Constrained Language Mode Bypass
useCases.value: Constrained Language Mode limits PowerShell attack surface. Detecting bypasses reveals attackers escalating from restricted to full-language mode for malware execution.

useCases.title: Windows Firewall Rule Tampering
useCases.value: Attackers disable or modify firewall rules to enable lateral movement, C2 communication, and data exfiltration. Rule changes outside maintenance windows indicate compromise.

useCases.title: BITS Transfer Abuse Detection
useCases.value: Background Intelligent Transfer Service (BITS) is abused by malware for stealthy downloads and persistence. Monitoring BITS jobs detects LOLBin-based attacks.

useCases.title: COM Object Hijacking Detection
useCases.value: COM hijacking replaces legitimate COM objects with malicious ones for persistence and privilege escalation. It's a stealthy technique that survives reboots.

useCases.title: LSASS Memory Protection Monitoring
useCases.value: LSASS contains credentials in memory. Monitoring LSASS access attempts and protection status detects credential dumping tools like Mimikatz.

useCases.title: Logon Session Anomalies (Type 3 / Network Logon)
useCases.value: Network logons (Type 3) from unexpected sources indicate lateral movement with stolen credentials. Baselining normal patterns reveals compromised accounts.

useCases.title: WMI Persistence Detection
useCases.value: WMI event subscriptions provide fileless persistence that survives reboots. Detecting WMI persistence reveals advanced persistent threats.

useCases.title: NIC Teaming & Network Adapter Failures (Windows)
useCases.value: NIC teaming provides network redundancy for servers. Adapter failures reduce redundancy and can cause outages if the remaining NIC also fails.

useCases.title: ASR (Attack Surface Reduction) Rule Monitoring
useCases.value: ASR rules block common attack techniques (Office macro code, credential theft, ransomware). Monitoring ASR ensures rules are enforced and detects blocked attacks.

useCases.title: Registry Run Key Persistence Monitoring
useCases.value: Registry Run keys are the most common persistence mechanism for malware. Monitoring autostart registry locations detects new malware installations.

useCases.title: BitLocker Recovery & Compliance Monitoring
useCases.value: BitLocker protects data at rest. Monitoring recovery events detects unauthorized hardware changes, and compliance tracking ensures all endpoints are encrypted.

useCases.title: DNS Client Query Anomalies
useCases.value: Monitoring DNS queries from Windows clients reveals C2 beacons, DNS tunneling, and DGA-based malware communicating with attacker infrastructure.

useCases.title: Local Account Creation & Modification
useCases.value: Creating local accounts is a persistence technique. On domain-joined systems, local account creation is rare and suspicious.

useCases.title: Token Manipulation / Privilege Escalation
useCases.value: Token manipulation (impersonation, token duplication) allows attackers to escalate privileges. Detecting abuse of SeImpersonatePrivilege catches potato-style attacks.

useCases.title: Process Injection Detection (Sysmon)
useCases.value: Process injection hides malicious code inside legitimate processes. Detecting injection techniques (CreateRemoteThread, APC, process hollowing) catches advanced malware.

useCases.title: Cluster Shared Volume (CSV) Health
useCases.value: Cluster Shared Volumes underpin Hyper-V and SQL Server failover clusters. CSV failures cause VM/database unavailability across the cluster.

useCases.title: DCOM Activation Failures
useCases.value: DCOM failures break distributed applications, WMI remote management, and SCCM client operations. Monitoring identifies misconfigured permissions and network issues.

useCases.title: Automatic Windows Update Compliance
useCases.value: Unpatched systems are the primary attack surface. Tracking Windows Update status across all systems ensures timely patching and compliance reporting.

useCases.title: Service Account Logon Anomalies
useCases.value: Compromised service accounts grant persistent access and often have elevated privileges. Detecting anomalous service account behavior catches credential theft early.

useCases.title: Sysmon Driver/Image Load Monitoring
useCases.value: Monitoring driver and DLL loads catches rootkits, vulnerable drivers, and DLL side-loading attacks that evade process-level monitoring.

useCases.title: Scheduled Task Modification for Persistence
useCases.value: Modifying existing scheduled tasks is stealthier than creating new ones. Attackers replace legitimate task actions to achieve persistence without new artifacts.

useCases.title: Windows Print Spooler Health
useCases.value: Spooler service state, queue depth, and stalled print jobs affect printing availability. Print Spooler failures block all printing on the host.

useCases.title: Windows Scheduled Task Failures
useCases.value: Detect tasks that failed to run or returned non-zero result codes. Indicates missed backups, sync jobs, or automation failures.

useCases.title: Windows WMI Repository Health
useCases.value: WMI corruption breaks many monitoring agents, SCCM, and management tools. Detecting broken WMI enables early remediation before dependent systems fail.

useCases.title: Windows Pending Reboot Detection
useCases.value: Detect servers waiting for reboot after Windows updates. Pending reboots cause inconsistent behavior and can block security patch application.

useCases.title: System Resource Monitoring
useCases.value: Endpoint performance visibility helps IT support triage user complaints and identify machines needing replacement or upgrades.

useCases.title: FileVault Encryption Status
useCases.value: Unencrypted endpoints are a data breach risk if lost or stolen. Compliance requirement for most security frameworks (SOC2, ISO27001, PCI).

useCases.title: Gatekeeper and SIP Status
useCases.value: Disabled Gatekeeper or System Integrity Protection weakens macOS security posture. May indicate developer override or tampering.

useCases.title: Software Update Compliance
useCases.value: Unpatched macOS endpoints are vulnerable. Tracking update levels across the fleet supports vulnerability management.

useCases.title: Application Crash Monitoring
useCases.value: Frequent application crashes degrade user experience and may indicate malware, resource issues, or incompatible software.

useCases.title: macOS Gatekeeper and XProtect Status
useCases.value: Verify Gatekeeper and XProtect are enabled and definitions are current. Disabled or outdated security controls increase malware risk.

useCases.title: Hardware Sensor Monitoring
useCases.value: Temperature, voltage, and fan speed anomalies predict impending hardware failures before they cause unplanned downtime.

useCases.title: RAID Degradation Alerts
useCases.value: A degraded RAID has lost redundancy — another disk failure means data loss. Requires immediate attention.

useCases.title: Power Supply Failure
useCases.value: Lost power supply redundancy means a single PSU failure away from an unplanned outage. Replacement needs to happen before the remaining PSU fails.

useCases.title: Predictive Disk Failure
useCases.value: SMART attributes can predict disk failure days or weeks in advance, enabling proactive replacement during maintenance windows.

useCases.title: Firmware Version Compliance
useCases.value: Outdated firmware may have security vulnerabilities or known bugs. Fleet-wide firmware tracking supports patch management.

useCases.title: Memory ECC Error Trending
useCases.value: Correctable ECC errors that increase over time strongly predict impending DIMM failure. Proactive replacement avoids unrecoverable memory errors and system crashes.

useCases.title: BMC Out-of-Band Connectivity Health
useCases.value: BMC (IPMI/iDRAC/iLO) loss prevents remote power, console, and sensor access. Early detection ensures out-of-band management remains available for recovery.

useCases.title: PCIe Link Width and Speed Degradation
useCases.value: PCIe links that downgrade (e.g. x16→x8) indicate slot or cable issues. Affects GPU, NVMe, and HBA performance and can precede full failure.

useCases.title: Out-of-Band Sensor Threshold Breach (IPMI)
useCases.value: IPMI sensor events (temperature, voltage, fan) indicate environmental or hardware problems before they cause crashes. Critical for datacenter and server health.

useCases.title: Disk Controller and HBA Health
useCases.value: RAID/HBA controller errors and degraded state often precede array failure. Early visibility enables planned maintenance and avoids data loss.

useCases.title: Boot Order and UEFI/BIOS Configuration Drift
useCases.value: Unauthorized or accidental boot order changes can prevent systems from booting from the correct disk or PXE. Tracking supports change audit and recovery.
